title: Stomp-off signals
summary: Leaders signal the last chorus, and hand signals mark break lengths.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Another thing I noticed when I first heard New Orleans bands is that you don't notice that in other cities and up north is the stomping off business.
Oh, they always did that down in the old time.
Knock off to go out. Yeah, I remember.
Yeah. And before they got there, you give it that.
Now, where should that, when you knock off, or whatever you call it, where should that be? Right before the last course, or as you start the last course?
Where's the correct place? I mean, knocking off to go out? Yeah, to go out. Well, I mean, everybody having fun. If the leader don't knock off, I could continue playing. Yeah.
I mean, when should he give you that signal? Right before the last course?
Right before the last course. Right before you start. Oh, now, probably the tune might run. The way the tune might run might be the last eight.
Could be then. Sometimes he stops.
The majority of the time at the last course.
Yeah, the whole chorus.
I think we're the honest one using that now. We do it sometimes.

But I wonder if the leader gave the stomp in the middle of the chorus there. Well, it'll go out. And that's the end. Yeah, when he do that. That's the end. Right there. You wouldn't play another one after that if you were about halfway through and he stopped it. And you finish up then. That's right. Because I thought it might be a signal then to go another whole course. I didn't know if they had any special signal.
It's a pretty good thing for cats just getting back to what we were talking about. You know, you call people up on the phone and you just get together. So you've got to ask some kind of rude things.
They don't know those things other parts of the country. I've ever heard.
We use a whole lot of old time things out there. Do this.
Oh, yeah. Hold it.
Another one.
Hold the hand.
Put this on him. That's four bar. Four bar break.
Four fingers means a four bar break.
Four bar tag for him. Oh, yeah. Alright, that's football tag for him. And we'll do that. That's football tag for him and we're going to play the last eight.
